name: dnssector
reason: DNSSector::parse validates the whole message (including compressed names inside CNAME/MX RDATA) and the RR iterators return owner name, type, class, TTL and A/AAAA addresses, but other RDATA only as raw bytes (RawRRData::Data). The crate has no public API returning the CNAME target, MX preference or MX exchange as values (Compress::copy_uncompressed_name yields wire-format labels only), so the control's CNAME and MX answers would have to be decoded by the harness.

name: microdns
reason: Minimal resolver library: its public helpers parse the header and answer records, but the question section is only skipped (skip_question) and its name, type and class are not returned, and authority/additional handling is left to callers. The control's question cannot be reported from the library.

name: smoltcp
found_by: registry search hit (crates.io sorted by recent downloads)
reason: smoltcp::wire::dns (Packet, Question, Record::parse) is a documented public wire API, but RecordData decodes only A and AAAA: CNAME stays as the raw (possibly compressed) name bytes and MX falls into Other(type, raw bytes), with no exported decoder for names inside RDATA, so the control's CNAME and MX answers would have to be decoded by the harness. The crate is a TCP/IP stack; its count covers all protocols.

name: webrtc-mdns
found_by: registry search hit (crates.io sorted by recent downloads)
reason: The public module webrtc_mdns::message (a Rust port of Go's golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage via Pion mDNS, with typed A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/NS/PTR/SOA/SRV/TXT bodies) has Message::unpack(&mut self, &[u8]), but neither the README (which documents only the mDNS conn) nor any rustdoc comment documents it: every item in message/ carries plain // comments, so docs.rs shows bare signatures. Same rule as PHP yswery/dns: a public but undocumented entry point stays a lead. Family would be the x/net dnsmessage port already selected in Go.
